text:
anya: Hi all 10I just opened my first PR for the payments webhook validation (branch feat/payments/webhook-validate). Quick questions about our expected PR checklist and whether we should include tiny refactor commits or squash everything.

kevin: Welcome, anya! :wave: Short answers: include granular commits while you iterate, but the final merge should keep the main branch tidy. We usually do either a squash+merge for small feature PRs or an explicit rebase+merge for multi-commit features.

rahul: Add to that 3we have a lightweight PR template. Please fill the "Testing" and "Migration" sections. Also paste the ticket link (PAY-314) at the top.

anya: Thanks. What's the exact format you prefer for commit messages? We have a few small scopes touched (payments, auth).

kevin: We follow this convention: `scope(area): short summary`
Examples: `payments(webhook): validate signature and reject bad payloads` or `auth: tighten token parsing`. Keep subject under 72 chars, and add a short body if there are non-obvious decisions.

rahul: For branching, prefix feature branches with `feat/` and bugfixes with `fix/`. For work-in-progress use `wip/` or mark the PR as draft.

anya: Got a lint failure locally when running pre-commit. Are there any additional linters beyond ruff/black?

kevin: ruff + black + isort. Run `pre-commit run --all-files` after installing hooks. We also have `make lint` that runs everything. If CI shows a formatting-only failure, it's fine to push a follow-up commit with `chore(format): apply formatting` rather than mixing code changes in the same commit.

rahul: CI expectations: unit tests, typecheck, and integration tests must pass. If the integration job flakes, mark the PR with `ci-flake` and ping #eng-oncall.

anya: How do reviewers expect test coverage to be documented? I added a small unit test but coverage dropped a hair.

kevin: Add a short note in the PR body: which new tests were added and what they assert. If coverage drops <0.5% due to non-critical paths that's usually fine, but call it out.

rahul: Also include manual steps to exercise the change locally in the PR (commands and sample payloads). Example: 
```
make dev
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/webhook -H "X-Signature: <sig>" -d '{"event":"payment.succeeded"}'
```

anya: Do we have a policy for changing API shapes? I made a tiny optional field change in the validation logic but didn't change the response format.

kevin: Any API contract change needs an explicit note and product approval. Optional internal validation tweaks are OK; changing the contract or response body requires a changelog entry and product ping.

rahul: If the PR touches infra (k8s manifests, helm), add the `infra` label and mention @infra-lead for one more review.

anya: One last: what's the etiquette for force-pushes? I had to rebase and resolved conflicts locally.

kevin: Force-pushes are fine on draft branches or before a review starts. Once reviewers are added avoid force-pushes unless you call them out in the thread and re-request review. Use `--force-with-lease` not `--force`.

dev-tools-bot: tip: to request reviewers again after pushing, comment `@dev-tools-bot request-review` to trigger the request.

anya: Perfect, I'll update the PR body with the checklist and the local test commands, run pre-commit, and mark ready. Thanks for the help! :pray:

kevin: Happy to pair if you want a quick rebase walkthrough.

rahul: Nice work, and welcome aboard! :tada:
